title: Separatedness from an affine open cover with affine overlaps and surjective restriction maps
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:V\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $V=\bigcup_{a\in A}V_a$ a covering of $V$ by affine open subschemes. Suppose that for all $a,b\in A$ the open subscheme $V_a\cap V_b$ is affine and the ring map $\mathcal O_V(V_a)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_V(V_b)\to\mathcal O_V(V_a\cap V_b)$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x|_{V_a\cap V_b}\cdot y|_{V_a\cap V_b}$, is surjective. Then $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], i.e. its diagonal $V\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), part (2), lines 4157-4175, specialized to an affine base $S$ (every pair of affine opens of $V$ maps into the common affine open $S$)

proof.text: Notation and an affine open cover of $V\times_SV$. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $A_a=\mathcal O_V(V_a)$, $C_{ab}=\mathcal O_V(V_a\cap V_b)$, and let $p,q:V\times_SV\to V$ be the two projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Each $A_a$ is an $R$-algebra via $R=\mathcal O_S(S)\xrightarrow{f^\sharp}\mathcal O_V(V)\to A_a$, and $V_a\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ over $S$ since $V_a$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $a,b\in A$ put $W_{ab}=p^{-1}(V_a)\cap q^{-1}(V_b)$, an open subset of $V\times_SV$. (i) The $W_{ab}$ cover $V\times_SV$: for a point $z$ choose $a$ with $p(z)\in V_a$ and $b$ with $q(z)\in V_b$; then $z\in W_{ab}$. (ii) By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with the open $U=S$ of the base and the opens $V_a,V_b$ of the two factors, $f(V_a),f(V_b)\subseteq S$), the canonical morphism $V_a\times_SV_b\to V\times_SV$ is an open immersion with image $W_{ab}$, compatibly with the projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $V_a\times_SV_b\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_a\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}A_b\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_a\otimes_RA_b)$ with the projections becoming $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and $y\mapsto1\otimes y$. Hence $W_{ab}$ is an affine open of $V\times_SV$ and there is a ring isomorphism $\mathcal O(W_{ab})\cong A_a\otimes_RA_b$ under which $p^\sharp(x)|_{W_{ab}}\mapsto x\otimes1$ for $x\in A_a$ (here $p^\sharp:\mathcal O_V(V_a)\to\mathcal O(p^{-1}V_a)$) and $q^\sharp(y)|_{W_{ab}}\mapsto1\otimes y$ for $y\in A_b$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), proof of part (2), lines 4198-4215: 'the collection of affine opens $U\times_SV$ ... form an affine open covering of $X\times_SX$ (see e.g. Lemma 01JS)', and the proof of part (1): '$U\times_SV=U\times_WV=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RB)$ is an affine open of $X\times_SX$' (Lemma 01JR lemma-open-fibre-product, Lemma 01JQ lemma-fibre-product-affines); the covering claim of 01JS is written out in (i) directly

proof.text: Inverse image under the diagonal. Let $\Delta:V\to V\times_SV$ be the diagonal, the morphism with $p\circ\Delta=q\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_V$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. For $v\in V$ we have $\Delta(v)\in W_{ab}$ iff $p(\Delta(v))=v\in V_a$ and $q(\Delta(v))=v\in V_b$; so $\Delta^{-1}(W_{ab})=V_a\cap V_b$, which is affine by hypothesis, with ring $C_{ab}$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), proof of part (2), lines 4198-4215: '$U\cap V=\Delta_{X/S}^{-1}(U\times_SV)$'; also the proof of Lemma 01KO (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated): '$\Delta_{X/S}^{-1}(V_j\times_{U_i}V_{j\prime})=V_j\cap V_{j\prime}$'

proof.text: The ring map induced by $\Delta$ over $W_{ab}$. Let $\Delta^\sharp_{W_{ab}}:\mathcal O(W_{ab})\to\mathcal O_V(\Delta^{-1}W_{ab})=C_{ab}$ be the ring map induced by $\Delta$ (step 2). For $x\in A_a$, functoriality of pulling back sections gives $\Delta^\sharp(p^\sharp(x)|_{W_{ab}})=(p\circ\Delta)^\sharp(x)|_{V_a\cap V_b}=x|_{V_a\cap V_b}$, and likewise $\Delta^\sharp(q^\sharp(y)|_{W_{ab}})=y|_{V_a\cap V_b}$ for $y\in A_b$. Since $\Delta^\sharp$ is a ring homomorphism and $x\otimes y=(x\otimes1)(1\otimes y)$, under the identification of step 1 the map $\Delta^\sharp_{W_{ab}}$ is $\varphi_{ab}:A_a\otimes_RA_b\to C_{ab}$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x|_{V_a\cap V_b}\cdot y|_{V_a\cap V_b}$ (it is determined on the pure tensors, which span $A_a\otimes_RA_b$ additively).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), proof of part (2), lines 4198-4215: 'writing $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ ... the composition $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B\to A\otimes_RB\to C$' (the identification of $\Delta$ over $U\times_SV$ with this ring map is left implicit there and written out here)

proof.text: Surjectivity. The ring map $\pi:A_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A_b\to A_a\otimes_RA_b$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$ (well defined since the defining relations of $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ hold in $\otimes_R$), is surjective because its image contains every pure tensor and is additively closed. The composite $\varphi_{ab}\circ\pi$ is $x\otimes y\mapsto x|_{V_a\cap V_b}\cdot y|_{V_a\cap V_b}$, the map assumed surjective in the statement. Hence $\varphi_{ab}$ is surjective.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), proof of part (2), lines 4198-4215: 'the assumption (b) means that the composition $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B\to A\otimes_RB\to C$ is surjective. Hence $A\otimes_RB\to C$ is surjective'

proof.text: Conclusion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], part (2), to $h=\Delta:V\to V\times_SV$ and the covering of $V\times_SV$ by the affine opens $W_{ab}$ (step 1): for every $(a,b)$ the open $\Delta^{-1}(W_{ab})=V_a\cap V_b$ is affine (step 2) and $\Delta^\sharp_{W_{ab}}$ is surjective (steps 3 and 4). Hence $\Delta$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], i.e. $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].
